external:core/demographic-targeting-capa.description: Product-scoped demographic execution capability. This declaration is product-scoped because one seller may route products through different ad servers. Buyers compare a requested canonical predicate with these capabilities before purchase; sellers MUST reject predicates they cannot compile exactly. A buyer that chooses a supported alternative submits that predicate as a new request.

age.description: Age-targeting execution available for this product.

execution_modes.description: Ways this product can execute canonical age intent. continuous_bounds accepts canonical predicates whose explicit integer bounds fall between min_supported_age and max_supported_age, inclusive; omitted bounds additionally require the corresponding supports_unbounded_min or supports_unbounded_max flag. enumerated_intervals accepts exact unions of the declared intervals; signals resolves through signals carrying authoritative demographic_predicate metadata.

min_supported_age.description: Lowest integer accepted as an explicit min or max bound by continuous_bounds. This limit does not replace an omitted min: omission means no lower age restriction. Required when that execution mode is declared.

max_supported_age.description: Highest integer accepted as an explicit min or max bound by continuous_bounds. This limit does not replace an omitted max: omission means no upper age restriction, so a request such as min 65 remains 65+ even when max_supported_age is 65. Required when that execution mode is declared.

supports_unbounded_min.description: Whether continuous_bounds accepts a predicate with min omitted. When true, the omitted min means no lower age restriction and MUST NOT be replaced by min_supported_age. When false, the seller MUST reject open-lower predicates. Required when continuous_bounds is declared.

supports_unbounded_max.description: Whether continuous_bounds accepts a predicate with max omitted. When true, the omitted max means no upper age restriction and MUST NOT be replaced by max_supported_age; for example, min 65 remains 65+. When false, the seller MUST reject open-upper predicates. Required when continuous_bounds is declared.

unknown_handling.description: How this product handles people whose age is unavailable. selectable honors either include_unknown value; always_excluded supports only false; always_included supports only true. A seller MUST reject a request incompatible with this declaration rather than silently changing it.

supported_bases.description: User-level age determination bases this product can use for exact execution. Sellers MUST publish only bases whose provenance they can preserve and audit; they MUST NOT infer a basis from an opaque platform age bucket. When omitted, the product makes no basis-aware targeting commitment and MUST reject requests that specify accepted_bases.

supported_verification_methods.description: Age verification methods available when supported_bases contains verified. This is an availability declaration only: a method must still establish the entire requested age predicate. Threshold-only methods such as World ID cannot establish an arbitrary bounded range.

intervals.description: Seller-owned age intervals available to enumerated_intervals execution. Bounds are authoritative capability data, not a protocol-wide bucket taxonomy. Exact compilation may union adjacent intervals but MUST NOT introduce gaps or extra ages.

interval_id.description: Seller-scoped interval identifier echoed in demographic targeting readback.

external:enums/age-determination-basis.j.title: Age Determination Basis
external:enums/age-determination-basis.j.description: User-level bases that may resolve age for demographic targeting execution. Population estimates are deliberately absent because aggregate composition cannot establish an individual impression's age.

enumDescriptions.verified: The user's applicable age claim was established through an age-assurance or identity-verification method.
enumDescriptions.declared: The user supplied an age, date of birth, or threshold affirmation without independent verification.
enumDescriptions.inferred: The user's age was predicted from behavior, attributes, or another model.

external:enums/age-verification-method.j.title: Age Verification Method
external:enums/age-verification-method.j.description: Methods for verifying user age for compliance. Does not include 'inferred' as it is not accepted for regulatory compliance.

external:core/targeting-overlay-support..title: Targeting Overlay Support
external:core/targeting-overlay-support..description: Product-scoped package targeting dimensions that may be supplied or changed after discovery. This is the seller response shape and may disclose seller limits such as max_values_per_package and max_packages. Product.overlay_support is the binding selectable-targeting contract: presence means the seller can apply protocol-valid values within the declared systems, countries, values, types, versions, and limits. Inherent product coverage alone does not satisfy a future-support requirement. Support does not guarantee inventory or a value-specific forecast before values are supplied; fixed prices and floors remain binding for supported selections. geo_regions and geo_regions_exclude are independent: structured support either exhaustively declares every value active in the seller's support snapshot for a country or lists the exact finite selectable subset. Buyer minimums use targeting-overlay-requirements.json. A requirement value of true matches true or any valid support object; an object requirement matches true or a containing support object. Every valid structured support object represents a positive capability; empty, extension-only, and false-only objects are invalid. Unrequested object fields and numeric seller limits do not participate in matching.

max_packages.description: Optional maximum number of independently targeted packages the seller will create from this configured product.

placeCatalogSupport.description: Selectable country/type pairs and catalog versions for one identifier system.

current_version.description: Version applied when a later package overlay omits system_version. Must be present in system_versions.

system_versions.description: Exact catalog versions selectable on later package overlays.

x-adcp-validation.description: JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express scalar membership in a sibling array; conformance tooling MUST verify current_version is present in system_versions.

placeSupport.description: Binding permission to select named-place values later, keyed first by identifier system and then by country to avoid namespace and place-type collisions.

max_packages.description: Optional maximum number of independently place-targeted packages the seller will create from this configured product.

anyOf.description: Canonical browser families that may be selected on packages later. This is executable targeting capability, not a guarantee of inventory for every family.

external:core/geo-place-type.json.title: Geographic Place Type
external:core/geo-place-type.json.description: Canonical place classification. Registered tokens have protocol-defined meanings. Catalog-specific classifications without a registered mapping MUST use an absolute HTTPS URI controlled by the vocabulary owner; consumers compare URI types as exact opaque strings.

external:core/geo-place-system.json.title: Geographic Place Identifier System
external:core/geo-place-system.json.description: Collision-safe identifier namespace for geographic places. Registered tokens have protocol-defined semantics. Unregistered systems MUST use an absolute HTTPS URI controlled by the catalog owner; consumers compare URI systems as exact opaque strings.

external:enums/match-type.json.title: Match Type
external:enums/match-type.json.description: Keyword targeting match type. broad: ads may serve on queries semantically related to the keyword. phrase: ads serve when the query contains the keyword phrase. exact: ads serve only when the query matches the keyword exactly.

enumDescriptions.broad: Ads may serve on queries semantically related to the keyword
enumDescriptions.phrase: Ads serve when the query contains the keyword phrase in order
enumDescriptions.exact: Ads serve only when the query matches the keyword exactly

external:enums/browser-family.json.title: Browser Family
external:enums/browser-family.json.description: Portable browser families for targeting the impression delivery and rendering environment, not a post-click landing-page browser. Values identify browser families, not versions or seller-native browser IDs, and MUST NOT be inferred solely from operating system, device, web/mobile-web inventory, or placement. android_webview means an impression reliably classified as rendering in Android WebView. other means a seller-recognized browser family that is not explicitly enumerated; unknown means the seller cannot classify the browser into a recognized family.

external:core/geo-region-support.json.title: Geographic Region Support
external:core/geo-region-support.json.description: Country- and value-aware support for selecting canonical ISO 3166-2 subdivisions. all_values is exhaustive for the values active in the seller's support snapshot when the declaration is issued; it does not automatically include values introduced by a later catalog revision. values is an exact finite subset. In seller-wide capabilities, each declared value is individually supported within the response scope, but the declaration does not promise that values are jointly composable or available through the same execution route or account. In Product.overlay_support, the declared values form the binding set of executable targeting permissions for that Product, subject to its declared limits; support does not itself guarantee inventory for every selection.

countries.description: Selectable ISO subdivision values keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country.

all_values.description: Every protocol-valid ISO 3166-2 subdivision active in this declaration's support snapshot is selectable. Values introduced by a later catalog revision are not included automatically.

values.description: Exact finite selectable subset of ISO 3166-2 identifiers for this country.

catalog_version.description: Optional opaque ISO subdivision catalog or seller-mapping version that identifies the support snapshot. It is provenance, not part of subdivision identity.

as_of.description: Optional date on which the seller last validated this support declaration.

max_values_per_package.description: Optional maximum number of region values selectable on one package.

max_packages.description: Optional maximum number of independently region-targeted packages created from this configured product.

external:core/positive-postal-area-suppo.title: Positive Postal Area Support
external:core/positive-postal-area-suppo.description: Non-vacuous postal capability used for hard targeting requirements and product overlay support. At least one native system array or true-valued deprecated alias is required. The general seller-capabilities postal schema remains permissive for backward compatibility, but an empty or false-only map cannot satisfy a hard discovery requirement.

external:enums/transport-mode.json.title: Transport Mode
external:enums/transport-mode.json.description: Transportation modes for isochrone-based catchment area calculations. Determines how travel time translates to geographic reach.

enumDescriptions.walking: Pedestrian travel on walkable paths and sidewalks
enumDescriptions.cycling: Bicycle travel on roads and cycle paths
enumDescriptions.driving: Motor vehicle travel on road networks
enumDescriptions.public_transport: Public transit including bus, rail, metro, and ferry

external:core/product-targeting-resoluti.title: Product Targeting Resolution
external:core/product-targeting-resoluti.description: Discovery-only targeting resolution bound to a configured Product. modifications sparsely disclose product-specific differences from get_products.targeting_overlay. Request-level brief interpretation and package execution details are not valid here.

modifications.description: Ordered changes applied to the requested targeting_overlay. Sellers apply entries in array order and MUST validate the complete resulting overlay before returning the product.

effective_targeting_digest.description: Optional digest of the canonical effective targeting overlay. Until AdCP defines a cross-implementation canonicalization algorithm, this value is an opaque seller audit handle and buyers MUST NOT attempt to reproduce or compare it across sellers.

external:core/targeting-modification.jso.title: Targeting Modification
external:core/targeting-modification.jso.description: Sparse, buyer-reviewable change from targeting requested in get_products to targeting bound to a returned configured product. Entries are applied in array order to the original targeting_overlay; after every entry, the complete result MUST validate against targeting.json. A seller MUST NOT emit two replace operations for the same path or combine replace and remove_values on the same path. Selecting the configured product_id accepts the ordered result.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to one complete targeting value relative to targeting_overlay, for example /demographics/age. Array indexes are forbidden by protocol semantics even if syntactically valid JSON Pointer; target a stable whole dimension instead.

applied.description: Complete replacement value. It MUST validate against targeting.json at path; the seller then validates the complete effective overlay. This operation may narrow or broaden only as an explicit buyer-visible proposal.

path.description: Supported targeting field with string-set semantics. Postal-area paths identify their group with selector; direct top-level sets omit selector.

selector.description: Stable identity of exactly one postal-area group in the requested array. Required only for postal-area paths. Zero or multiple matches make the modification invalid.

values.description: Values removed from the requested set. Values absent from that set are invalid rather than no-ops.

external:core/audience-evidence.json.title: Audience Evidence
external:core/audience-evidence.json.description: An immutable, population-level claim about an inventory audience's composition, affinity, or estimated reach. This object is discovery and planning evidence only: it MUST NOT be interpreted as an exact targeting predicate, proof that any particular impression belongs to the audience, or legal-age verification.

evidence_id.description: Stable provider-scoped identifier for the logical evidence series across versions.

snapshot_id.description: Seller-scoped immutable snapshot identifier. It MUST never be reused for different content.

version.description: Provider version of this evidence snapshot.

content_digest.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical evidence core with content_digest and attestation_refs omitted. Attestation references are excluded so independently issued credentials can be attached without changing the immutable evidence snapshot and without creating a recursive digest. This digest is required even when snapshot_id is present so buyers can detect identifier reuse or catalog drift.

relationship.description: What the estimate says: population share, ratio to a baseline, or estimated reachable count.

value.description: Estimated relationship value, interpreted according to unit.

unit.description: composition uses fraction in [0,1], index uses ratio, and reach_estimate uses count.

baseline.description: Reference population against which the estimate was calculated.

evidence_type.description: Nature of the evidence. Independent verification is represented separately by attestation_refs and never inferred from this value.

resolution_method.description: Optional subject-resolution method used by the study or estimate. This describes population methodology, not a promise that the product can execute that resolution at serving time.

provider.description: Brand responsible for producing the evidence.

sample_size.description: Number of observations or respondents underlying the estimate, when applicable.

confidence.description: Provider-defined confidence score in [0,1]. Consumers MUST compare scores only when the provider's methodology makes them comparable.

last_updated.description: When the provider last produced or refreshed this immutable snapshot.

methodology_url.description: Documentation for interpreting the methodology. It is disclosure, not executable routing.

attestation_refs.description: Optional portable attestations about this exact evidence snapshot. Each subject MUST be resource type https://adcontextprotocol.org/claims/subjects/audience-evidence, subject.id MUST equal snapshot_id, and subject.content_digest MUST equal this evidence object's content_digest. Buyer references do not override evaluator issuer or resolver policy.

external:core/audience-characteristic.js.title: Audience Characteristic
external:core/audience-characteristic.js.description: A machine-comparable audience dimension and value or numeric range used in population-level audience evidence. The built-in `age` dimension uses completed years: scalar and set values and range bounds MUST be non-negative integers, and a range's min MUST be less than or equal to its max. Provider-defined dimensions SHOULD use an HTTPS URI and SHOULD identify their taxonomy so two similarly named dimensions are not assumed equivalent.

dimension.description: Canonical dimension name or HTTPS URI. AdCP 3.2 defines `age`; other values remain provider- or taxonomy-scoped.

value.description: Scalar or set value for the dimension.

range.description: Inclusive numeric interval. For dimension `age`, values are completed years and MUST be non-negative integers, and min MUST be less than or equal to max. JSON Schema enforces the age value and bound types; implementations enforce the relational min <= max constraint.

taxonomy.description: External system that defines the dimension or value. Taxonomy metadata is descriptive and does not create exact demographic targeting semantics.

label.description: Human-readable display label; never the comparison key.

external:enums/audience-evidence-methodo.title: Audience Evidence Methodology
external:enums/audience-evidence-methodo.description: How a population-level audience-evidence estimate was produced. This vocabulary is intentionally separate from signal-definition methodology: `projected` describes expansion of a sample or panel to a reference population and does not become a user-level signal-membership method.

external:enums/audience-subject-type.jso.title: Audience Subject Type
external:enums/audience-subject-type.jso.description: The kind of subject characterized by audience data or population-level evidence.

external:enums/audience-resolution-metho.title: Audience Resolution Method
external:enums/audience-resolution-metho.description: How subjects were resolved when producing a signal or population-level evidence estimate.

external:core/date-range.json.title: Date Range
external:core/date-range.json.description: A date range with inclusive start and end dates (ISO 8601 calendar dates). Used for billing periods, flight dates, and other calendar-day boundaries.

external:core/attestation-reference.json.title: Attestation Reference
external:core/attestation-reference.json.description: Portable, reference-first presentation of an independently issued claim. It identifies the claimed issuer, claim vocabulary, subject, and either a stable credential locator or an embedded credential. A presentation is a locator and claim hint, not proof or a trust decision. The evaluator remains verifier-of-record and MUST resolve or inspect the credential only under its published attestation capabilities and local trust policy.

claim_type.description: Open, absolute URI identifying the claim vocabulary. The URI is an identifier and need not be dereferenceable. AdCP does not maintain an enum of approved claims.

locator.description: Stable locator for resolving the credential. Credential URLs are permitted only when their canonical origin is allowlisted for the matched issuer. Issuer-scoped IDs name a resolver_id already published by the evaluator; the presentation cannot introduce a resolver URL.

credential_uri.description: HTTPS URI of the credential. Before any fetch, evaluators MUST match its canonical origin to credential_origins on the accepted issuer capability and then apply the attestation fetch contract.

credential_id.description: Stable credential identifier in the issuer's namespace. It is meaningful only together with issuer and resolver_id.

resolver_id.description: Identifier of a resolver already published in the matched accepted_issuers[].resolvers[] capability. A presenter cannot supply or override its URL.

embedded_credential.description: Optional inline credential for private, authenticated, or offline delivery. It may accompany locator or be the only delivery path. Its format must be supported by the evaluator, and the evaluator MUST verify the credential exactly as it would a resolved credential.

format.description: Open, absolute URI identifying the credential/proof format. AdCP does not impose a universal issuer payload schema.

value.description: Credential encoded as a JSON object or a compact string, according to format.

content_digest.description: Optional SHA-256 digest pin for the exact credential bytes, formatted as sha256:<lowercase hex>. The credential format defines its canonical byte representation. A mismatch is invalid and MUST NOT fall back to the unpinned credential. REQUIRED when both locator and embedded_credential are present; both byte representations MUST match this digest.

credential_version.description: Optional issuer-defined credential version hint. It is advisory; the resolved credential is authoritative.

validity_hint.description: Optional planning-time validity hint copied from issuer metadata. Evaluators MUST use the resolved or embedded credential's signed validity and revocation state as authoritative.

verify_agent.description: Optional presenter nomination of a verifier already published by the evaluator. This is a representation, not routing authority: agent_url MUST match an accepted_verifiers[] entry after canonicalization, and the evaluator may choose another accepted verifier or verify locally.

external:core/attestation-issuer.json.title: Attestation Issuer
external:core/attestation-issuer.json.description: Canonical identity of the party that issued an attestation credential. The discriminator selects an existing AdCP identity when one exists and falls back to an HTTPS origin for other attestors. This identity is a claim carried by the presentation; evaluators MUST match it against their configured trust policy and verify it from the resolved or embedded credential before relying on it.

type.description: The issuer is identified by an AdCP BrandRef.
The issuer is an AdCP agent identified by its canonical HTTPS endpoint.

agent_url.description: Canonical HTTPS endpoint of the issuing agent. Evaluators compare it using AdCP URL canonicalization rules.

type.description: The issuer is identified by a canonical HTTPS origin because no AdCP brand or agent identity applies.

origin.description: Canonical HTTPS origin with no path, query, fragment, or userinfo. This identifies the issuer; it does not authorize a fetch.

external:core/attestation-subject.json.title: Attestation Subject
external:core/attestation-subject.json.description: Typed identity of the entity or object an attestation credential is about. Brand and agent subjects reuse canonical AdCP identities. Other resources use an open, URI-namespaced resource_type plus an identifier whose namespace is explicit. Evaluators MUST compare the resolved credential subject to this complete typed identity, not to id alone.

agent_url.description: Canonical HTTPS endpoint of the agent the claim concerns.

resource_type.description: Open, absolute URI naming the subject vocabulary, such as https://adcontextprotocol.org/claims/subjects/signal. AdCP does not maintain an exhaustive enum.

namespace.description: Absolute URI identifying the namespace in which id is unique. This may be an AdCP agent endpoint, a catalog origin, or a domain-specific namespace URI.

id.description: Stable identifier for the subject within namespace. It MUST NOT be compared without resource_type and namespace.

content_digest.description: Optional SHA-256 pin for the exact content or immutable snapshot identified by this resource subject. This is part of the complete typed subject identity and is distinct from AttestationReference.content_digest, which pins credential bytes.

external:core/audience-evidence-selectio.title: Audience Evidence Selection
external:core/audience-evidence-selectio.description: Decision readback for the exact immutable audience-evidence snapshot used in product recommendation, required eligibility, or package construction. Sellers MUST return this readback when evidence requirements affect inclusion or ranking even if get_products.fields omitted audience_evidence_selections. A constructed package MUST return a matching selection for every buyer audience_evidence_pin and for every evidence item used to satisfy package audience_evidence_requirements. Sellers MUST retain the full snapshot and evaluations for at least as long as the package remains available through media-buy read surfaces. AdCP 3.2 introduces no buyer-controlled snapshot URL: buyers cache product evidence, sellers retain the source record, and this digest-pinned readback detects catalog mutation. Full evidence may be embedded but is not required on every product or package.

decision_use.description: How this evidence affected the seller's decision. This is not targeting execution.

evidence.description: Optional inline immutable snapshot. Its identity, version, and digest MUST equal the surrounding fields.

attestation_evaluations.description: Exact reference/evaluation pairs used in the decision. The reference MUST be one of the selected evidence snapshot's attestation_refs, evaluation.reference_digest MUST equal the digest of that same reference, reference.subject.content_digest and evaluation.action_binding.action_digest MUST equal this selection's content_digest, evaluation.action_binding.action_id MUST equal snapshot_id, and action_type MUST be https://adcontextprotocol.org/actions/audience-evidence-evaluation.

action_id.$comment: x-entity deliberately omitted because the surrounding selection requires this value to equal snapshot_id.

external:core/attestation-evaluation.jso.title: Attestation Evaluation
external:core/attestation-evaluation.jso.description: Evaluator-of-record result for one portable attestation presentation. The result binds to the exact presentation through reference_digest and may also pin the credential bytes. It records evaluation, not issuer evidence: domain consumers attach this object to the governance context, evidence snapshot, rights decision, or other action that relied on it.

reference_digest.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme encoding of the complete AttestationReference, including embedded_credential when present. This prevents a result for one presentation from being replayed for another.

credential_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact resolved or embedded credential bytes according to proof_format. REQUIRED by the normative contract when outcome is verified, expired, revoked, invalid, subject_mismatch, or digest_mismatch; omitted when no credential bytes were obtained. For dual delivery, this is the resolved credential digest; reference_digest independently binds the embedded bytes.

proof_format.description: Absolute URI identifying the credential/proof format used to interpret and hash obtained credential bytes. REQUIRED whenever credential_digest is present.

outcome.description: Stable evaluation outcome. verified means all required issuer, signature, claim type, subject, consuming-action scope, validity, revocation, and digest checks passed under evaluator policy. subject_mismatch covers either a credential/presentation subject mismatch or a presentation/consuming-action subject mismatch. Other values are non-authoritative failures and MUST NOT be treated as verified.

evaluated_by.description: Canonical agent URL of the evaluator-of-record that produced this result, even when it delegated proof checking to an accepted verifier.

verifier_agent_url.description: Accepted verifier agent actually used, when verification was delegated. Omit for local verification or when no verifier was called.

reason_codes.description: Open, machine-readable reason identifiers supplied by the evaluator. Consumers MUST branch on outcome, not on free-form or evaluator-specific reason codes.

confidence.description: Optional evaluator-produced confidence in the normalized outcome on the AdCP 0–1 scale. This is evaluation output, never copied from an authoritative presenter field. Omit when the proof or evaluator does not support a meaningful confidence score.

revocation_checked_at.description: When the evaluator last checked authoritative revocation state. Its freshness is governed by proof format and evaluator policy.

valid_until.description: Upper bound on reuse of this evaluation, considering credential expiry, revocation-cache TTL, and evaluator policy. Consumers MUST re-evaluate after this time.

action_binding.description: Optional binding to the consuming action or readback. Domain consumers that rely on an evaluation MUST carry either an action id or an action digest so the result cannot be transplanted to an unrelated decision.

action_type.description: Absolute URI naming the action vocabulary, such as an AdCP governance-check or audience-evidence snapshot type.

action_id.description: Stable identifier of the consuming action within the domain consumer's namespace.
action_id.$comment: x-entity deliberately omitted because action_type determines which domain entity this identifier names.

action_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the domain-defined canonical action preimage.

external:core/vendor-metric-optimization.title: Vendor Metric Optimization
external:core/vendor-metric-optimization.description: Vendor-attested metric optimization capabilities for a product. Presence indicates the product supports `optimization_goals` with `kind: 'vendor_metric'` — i.e., the seller's bidding stack can steer delivery toward a specific vendor's metric. This is the optimization-side counterpart to `reporting_capabilities.vendor_metrics`, which declares which vendor metrics the product can *report*. The two are related but distinct: a product may be able to commit to reporting a vendor metric (the vendor's SDK fires on the inventory) without being able to optimize against it (the optimization signal isn't actionable in the seller's bidding stack). Each `supported_metrics` entry is the tuple `(vendor, metric_id)` plus the target kinds the seller supports for that pair. Buyers MUST set `vendor_metric` goals only against entries declared here; sellers MUST reject goals whose `(vendor, metric_id)` is not in `supported_metrics`, and MUST reject goals whose `target.kind` is not in the matching entry's `supported_targets`. Buyers SHOULD also verify the metric is in the vendor's published `measurement.metrics[]` catalog (the discovery-layer check — softened from MUST while measurement-vendor adoption of AdCP-conformant capability publication catches up; tightens to MUST at the next minor) and that the package's `committed_metrics[]` includes a matching `{ scope: 'vendor', vendor, metric_id }` entry (the reporting-coherence check — optimizing for a metric you don't commit to reporting is unverifiable). The `maximize_value` target kind from the `event` goal kind is intentionally excluded — it's monetary-only; a buyer wanting to maximize a vendor metric uses the target-less form of the `vendor_metric` goal. Precondition checks are seller-runtime, not JSON-Schema-enforceable: the schema's `required` only validates structural presence of `vendor` and `metric_id`.

supported_metrics.description: Vendor-defined metrics this product can steer delivery toward. Each entry pairs a vendor identity (BrandRef anchored on the vendor's `brand.json` `agents[type='measurement']`) with a `metric_id` from that vendor's published `measurement.metrics[]` catalog, plus the target kinds the seller supports for the pair. Semantic uniqueness key is `(vendor.domain, vendor.brand_id, metric_id)`; sellers MUST de-duplicate before publication. JSON Schema `uniqueItems` blocks exact-object duplicates; semantic deduplication on the BrandRef-domain key is a seller obligation.

external:core/vendor-metric-optimization.title: Vendor Metric Optimization Supported Metric
external:core/vendor-metric-optimization.description: One vendor-defined metric that a product can optimize toward. Identified by the tuple `(vendor, metric_id)` plus the supported target kinds for optimization goals.

vendor.description: Vendor that defines and computes this metric. The vendor's `brand.json` is the discovery anchor for the measurement agent (entry with `type: 'measurement'` in the `agents[]` array); the metric's definition, methodology, and unit live at that agent's `get_adcp_capabilities.measurement.metrics[]` and are not duplicated inline here. Same shape as the `vendor` field on `reporting_capabilities.vendor_metrics` for symmetry across optimization and reporting capability declarations.

metric_id.description: Identifier for the metric within the vendor's vocabulary (e.g., `attention_score`, `attention_seconds`, `gco2e_per_impression`, `awareness_lift`). MUST be present in the vendor's published `measurement.metrics[]` catalog.

supported_targets.description: Target kinds available for `vendor_metric` goals against this `(vendor, metric_id)` pair. Values match `target.kind` on the optimization goal. `cost_per` — target cost per metric unit (e.g., $0.05 per attention-second). `threshold_rate` — minimum per-impression value (e.g., attention_score ≥ 70). Only these target kinds are accepted — goals with unlisted target kinds will be rejected. A goal without a target implicitly maximizes the metric within budget — no declaration needed for that mode. When omitted, buyers can still set target-less vendor_metric goals.

external:core/measurement-readiness.json.title: Measurement Readiness
external:core/measurement-readiness.json.description: Per-product assessment of whether the buyer's event source setup is sufficient for the product's optimization capabilities. Sellers evaluate this in the context of the buyer's account — the same product may show different readiness for different buyers depending on their event source configuration.

status.description: Overall measurement readiness level for this product given the buyer's event setup. 'insufficient' means the product cannot optimize effectively with the current setup.

required_event_types.description: Event types this product needs for effective optimization. Buyers should ensure their event sources cover these types.

missing_event_types.description: Event types this product requires that the buyer has not configured. Empty or absent when all required types are covered.

issues.description: Actionable issues preventing full measurement readiness. Sellers should limit to the top 3-5 most actionable items. Buyer agents should sort by severity rather than relying on array position.

notes.description: Seller explanation of the readiness assessment, recommendations for improvement, or context about what the buyer needs to change.

external:enums/assessment-status.json.title: Assessment Status
external:enums/assessment-status.json.description: Standardized quality level for health and readiness assessments. Comparable across sellers — buyer agents should use this for cross-seller decisions.

enumDescriptions.insufficient: Setup incomplete or event quality too low — optimization cannot run
enumDescriptions.minimum: Functional but data quality limits optimization effectiveness
enumDescriptions.good: Meets quality thresholds for most optimization goals
enumDescriptions.excellent: Exceeds quality thresholds across all dimensions

external:core/diagnostic-issue.json.title: Diagnostic Issue
external:core/diagnostic-issue.json.description: An actionable issue detected during a health or readiness assessment. Used by event source health and measurement readiness to surface problems and recommendations.

severity.description: 'error': blocks optimization until resolved. 'warning': optimization works but effectiveness is reduced. 'info': suggestion for improvement.

message.description: Human/agent-readable description of the issue and how to resolve it.

enumDescriptions.app: Event occurred in a mobile or desktop app
enumDescriptions.phone_call: Event originated from a phone call
enumDescriptions.chat: Event originated from a chat conversation
enumDescriptions.email: Event originated from an email interaction
enumDescriptions.in_store: Event occurred at a physical retail location
enumDescriptions.system_generated: Event generated by an automated system

external:core/product-card-reference-ass.title: Product Card Reference Asset
external:core/product-card-reference-ass.description: Typed seller collateral for buyer-facing product cards. Each entry carries a semantic role (coverage_map, sample_render, etc.) and a canonical asset payload. Distinct from hero_image/carousel_images (display-oriented) and from core/reference-asset.json (creative-generation oriented).

role.description: Semantic role of this asset. coverage_map: geographic or audience reach visualization; sample_render: mockup of ad placement in context; environment_photo: photo of the physical or digital environment; media_kit: downloadable media kit or spec sheet; logo: seller or property logo; other: seller-defined role (provide role_label).

role_label.description: Human-readable label for the asset role. Required when role is 'other'; optional otherwise.

asset.description: The asset payload, discriminated on asset_type (image, video, markdown, url).

description.description: Optional human-readable context about this asset.

external:core/assets/video-asset.json.title: Video Asset
external:core/assets/video-asset.json.description: A hosted video file delivered directly (e.g., an MP4 you host), with URL and technical specifications including audio track properties. `width` and `height` are required because a hosted video file has intrinsic, native pixel dimensions that are known when the file is created. Tag-delivered video uses the separate `vast` asset, which carries no `width`/`height`: a VAST response resolves geometry per-`MediaFile` at serve time, so there is no single width/height for the ad. Aspect-ratio and size *constraints* (what a placement accepts) belong on the format/requirements layer, not on the asset.
external:core/assets/video-asset.json.$comment: Dimension policy is deliberate and differs by asset type: a hosted `video` asset requires width/height (intrinsic pixels of a concrete file), while the `vast` asset omits them entirely (renditions are selected per-MediaFile by the player at serve time). Do not infer that AdCP forces a single width/height onto all video — only onto hosted files.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a video asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

width.description: Width in pixels — the video file's intrinsic native width. Required: a hosted file always has concrete dimensions. (Tag-delivered video carries no width; see the `vast` asset.)

height.description: Height in pixels — the video file's intrinsic native height. Required: a hosted file always has concrete dimensions. (Tag-delivered video carries no height; see the `vast` asset.)

container_format.description: Video container format (mp4, webm, mov, etc.)

video_codec.description: Video codec used (h264, h265, vp9, av1, prores, etc.)

video_bitrate_kbps.description: Video stream bitrate in kilobits per second

frame_rate.description: Frame rate as string to preserve precision (e.g., '23.976', '29.97', '30')

hdr_format.description: HDR format if applicable, or 'sdr' for standard dynamic range

has_audio.description: Whether the video contains an audio track

audio_codec.description: Audio codec used (aac, aac_lc, he_aac, pcm, mp3, ac3, eac3, etc.)

audio_bitrate_kbps.description: Audio bitrate in kilobits per second

captions_url.description: URL to captions file (WebVTT, SRT, etc.)

transcript_url.description: URL to text transcript of the video content

audio_description_url.description: URL to audio description track for visually impaired users

provenance.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

external:enums/frame-rate-type.json.title: Frame Rate Type
external:enums/frame-rate-type.json.description: Whether the video uses a constant or variable frame rate. Broadcast and SSAI contexts require constant frame rate for seamless splicing.

enumDescriptions.constant: Constant frame rate (CFR) — each frame occupies an identical time interval
enumDescriptions.variable: Variable frame rate (VFR) — frame intervals may differ

external:enums/scan-type.json.title: Scan Type
external:enums/scan-type.json.description: Video scan method. Modern digital delivery requires progressive scan; interlaced is retained for broadcast legacy content.

enumDescriptions.progressive: All lines of each frame are drawn in sequence
enumDescriptions.interlaced: Alternating lines drawn in two passes per frame (legacy broadcast)

external:enums/gop-type.json.title: GOP Type
external:enums/gop-type.json.description: Group of Pictures structure. SSAI and broadcast require closed GOPs for clean splice points; open GOPs may produce artifacts at ad boundaries.

enumDescriptions.closed: Each GOP is independently decodable — required for SSAI and broadcast splicing
enumDescriptions.open: GOPs may reference frames from adjacent GOPs — not suitable for splicing

external:enums/moov-atom-position.json.title: Moov Atom Position
external:enums/moov-atom-position.json.description: Position of the moov atom in an MP4 container. 'start' enables progressive download without buffering the entire file; required for streaming ad delivery.

enumDescriptions.start: moov atom at beginning of file — enables progressive download and streaming delivery
enumDescriptions.end: moov atom at end of file — requires full download before playback can begin

external:enums/audio-channel-layout.json.title: Audio Channel Layout
external:enums/audio-channel-layout.json.description: Audio channel configuration for audio and video assets

external:core/assets/markdown-asset.json.title: Markdown Asset
external:core/assets/markdown-asset.json.description: Markdown-formatted text content following CommonMark specification

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a markdown asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

content.description: Markdown content following CommonMark spec with optional GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions

language.description: Optional language claim for this markdown. In a materialized creative localization variant, localized-creative-asset.json requires this value to use /schemas/core/locale-tag.json and conformance requires exact equality with the enclosing variant locale. General non-localized assets retain the legacy unconstrained string for compatibility.

markdown_flavor.description: Markdown flavor used. CommonMark for strict compatibility, GFM for tables/task lists/strikethrough.

allow_raw_html.description: Whether raw HTML blocks are allowed in the markdown. False recommended for security.

external:enums/markdown-flavor.json.title: Markdown Flavor
external:enums/markdown-flavor.json.description: Markdown specification flavors supported for text assets

external:core/assets/url-asset.json.title: URL Asset
external:core/assets/url-asset.json.$comment: Fallback table is also rendered in docs/creative/asset-types.mdx (URL Asset section). Keep the two in sync — schema description is the normative source for conformance tools; mdx is the human-readable copy.
external:core/assets/url-asset.json.description: URL reference asset. `url_type` declares the mechanism a receiver uses to invoke the URL (clickthrough vs. tracker_pixel vs. tracker_script) and is distinct from the URL's purpose, which the format declares in `url-asset-requirements.role` (clickthrough, landing_page, impression_tracker, click_tracker, viewability_tracker, third_party_tracker). Senders SHOULD include `url_type` on every URL asset. When `url_type` is absent, receivers SHOULD fall back to the format's `url-asset-requirements.role` per this mapping: clickthrough/landing_page → `clickthrough`; impression_tracker/click_tracker → `tracker_pixel`; viewability_tracker → `tracker_script` (OMID and equivalent verification SDKs require a <script> tag — firing them as a pixel produces no measurement); third_party_tracker → no safe fallback (mechanism is integration-specific — DV/IAS ship both pixel and script forms — receivers MAY reject or warn). When neither `url_type` nor a format-side `role` is available, receivers MUST NOT silently pick a mechanism; they SHOULD reject the manifest. Note: VAST/DAAST tag URLs are not URL assets — use `asset_type: "vast"` (or the dedicated tracker types pending RFC #2915), not `asset_type: "url"` with a tracker_pixel mechanism.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a URL asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

url.description: URL reference. May be a plain URI or an RFC 6570 URI template carrying AdCP universal macros (e.g., `{SKU}`, `{MEDIA_BUY_ID}`). Buyers MUST NOT pre-encode macro braces at sync time; the ad server URL-encodes substituted values at impression time. See docs/creative/universal-macros.mdx.

url_type.description: Mechanism a receiver uses to invoke this URL (distinct from purpose, which lives in `url-asset-requirements.role`): `clickthrough` for user click destination (landing page), `tracker_pixel` for impression/event tracking via HTTP request (fires GET, expects pixel/204 response), `tracker_script` for measurement SDKs that must load as a <script> tag (OMID verification, native event trackers using method:2). SHOULD be present on every URL asset; senders that omit it force the receiver into the role-based fallback described in this schema's top-level description.

description.description: Description of what this URL points to

provenance.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

external:enums/url-asset-type.json.title: URL Asset Type
external:enums/url-asset-type.json.description: Types of URL assets for tracking and click-through purposes

external:core/collection-selector.json.title: Collection Selector
external:core/collection-selector.json.description: References collections declared in an adagents.json. Buyers resolve full collection objects by fetching the adagents.json at the given domain and matching collection_ids against its collections array.

publisher_domain.description: Domain where the adagents.json declaring these collections is hosted (e.g., 'mrbeast.com'). The collections array in that file contains the authoritative collection definitions.

collection_ids.description: Collection IDs from the adagents.json collections array. Each ID must match a collection_id declared in that file.

external:core/installment.json.title: Installment
external:core/installment.json.description: A single bookable unit within a collection — one episode, issue, event, or rotation period. The parent collection's kind indicates how to interpret each installment: TV/podcast episodes, print issues, live event airings, newsletter editions, or DOOH rotation periods. Installments inherit collection-level fields they don't override: content_rating defaults to the collection's baseline, guest_talent is additive to the collection's recurring talent, and topics add context beyond the collection's genre.

installment_id.description: Unique identifier for this installment within the collection

collection_id.description: Parent collection reference. Required when the product spans multiple collections. Maps to a collection_id declared in one of the publishers' adagents.json files referenced by the product's collection selectors.

scheduled_at.description: When the installment airs or publishes (ISO 8601)

duration_seconds.description: Expected duration of the installment in seconds

flexible_end.description: Whether the end time is approximate (live events, sports)

valid_until.description: When this installment data expires and should be re-queried. Agents should re-query before committing budget to products with tentative installments.

content_rating.description: Installment-specific content rating. Overrides the collection's baseline content_rating when present.

topics.description: Content topics for this installment. Uses the same taxonomy as the collection's genre_taxonomy when present. Enables installment-level brand safety evaluation beyond content_rating.

special.description: Installment-specific event context. When present, this installment is anchored to a real-world event. Overrides the collection-level special when present.

guest_talent.description: Installment-specific guests and talent. Additive to the collection's recurring talent.

ad_inventory.description: Break-based ad inventory for this installment. For non-break formats (host reads, integrations), use product placements.

deadlines.description: Booking, cancellation, and material submission deadlines for this installment. Present when the installment has time-sensitive inventory that requires advance commitment or material delivery.

derivative_of.description: When this installment is a clip, highlight, or recap derived from a full installment. The source installment_id must reference an installment within the same response.

installment_id.description: The source installment this content is derived from

type.description: What kind of derivative content this is

enumDescriptions.tentative: May not happen (e.g., playoff Game 7 depends on Game 6)
enumDescriptions.live: Currently airing or streaming right now
enumDescriptions.postponed: Was scheduled but delayed to a future date

external:core/content-rating.json.title: Content Rating
external:core/content-rating.json.description: Content advisory rating using a specified rating system

external:enums/content-rating-system.jso.title: Content Rating System
external:enums/content-rating-system.jso.description: Rating systems for content advisory classifications

enumDescriptions.tv_parental: US TV Parental Guidelines (TV-Y, TV-Y7, TV-G, TV-PG, TV-14, TV-MA)
enumDescriptions.mpaa: Motion Picture Association film ratings (G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17)
enumDescriptions.esrb: Entertainment Software Rating Board (E, E10+, T, M, AO) — US/Canada
enumDescriptions.bbfc: British Board of Film Classification (U, PG, 12A, 12, 15, 18, R18)
enumDescriptions.acb: Australian Classification Board (G, PG, M, MA15+, R18+)
enumDescriptions.chvrs: Canadian Home Video Rating System (G, PG, 14A, 18A, R, A)
enumDescriptions.csa: Conseil superieur de l'audiovisuel / Arcom (-10, -12, -16, -18) — France
enumDescriptions.pegi: Pan European Game Information (3, 7, 12, 16, 18) — pan-European gaming
enumDescriptions.custom: Publisher-defined rating system with free-form values

external:core/special.json.title: Special
external:core/special.json.description: Event-anchored content tied to a real-world event or occasion. When present on a collection, indicates the collection is a special. When present on an installment, indicates that specific installment is event-anchored (overrides or supplements the collection-level special).

name.description: Name of the event (e.g., 'Olympics 2028', 'Super Bowl LXI')

ends.description: When the event ends (ISO 8601). Omit for single-day events.

external:enums/special-category.json.title: Special Category
external:enums/special-category.json.description: Category of special or event-anchored content

enumDescriptions.championship: Championship or tournament event (Super Bowl, World Cup, Olympics)

external:core/talent.json.title: Talent
external:core/talent.json.description: A person associated with a collection or installment, with an optional link to their brand.json identity

role.description: Role of this person on the collection or installment

name.description: Person's name as credited on the collection

brand_url.description: URL to this person's brand.json entry. Enables buyer agents to evaluate the talent's brand identity and associations.

external:enums/talent-role.json.title: Talent Role
external:enums/talent-role.json.description: Role of a person associated with a collection or installment

enumDescriptions.host: Primary host or anchor of the collection
enumDescriptions.guest: Guest appearing on a specific installment
enumDescriptions.creator: Collection creator or showrunner
enumDescriptions.producer: Executive or lead producer with on-screen presence
enumDescriptions.analyst: Color commentator or subject matter analyst

external:core/ad-inventory-config.json.title: Ad Inventory Configuration
external:core/ad-inventory-config.json.description: Break-based ad inventory configuration for an installment. Describes the ad breaks available within the content. For non-break ad formats (host reads, integrations, sponsorships), use product placements instead.

expected_breaks.description: Number of planned ad breaks in the installment

total_ad_seconds.description: Total seconds of ad time across all breaks

max_ad_duration_seconds.description: Maximum duration in seconds for a single ad within a break. Buyers need this to know whether their creative fits.

unplanned_breaks.description: Whether ad breaks are dynamic and driven by live conditions (sports timeouts, election coverage). When false, all breaks are pre-defined.

supported_formats.description: Ad format types supported in breaks (e.g., 'video', 'audio', 'display')

external:core/installment-deadlines.json.title: Installment Deadlines
external:core/installment-deadlines.json.description: Deadlines associated with a bookable installment. Applies to any channel where inventory is tied to a scheduled unit: print issues, podcast episodes, linear TV airings, influencer posts, DOOH rotations.

booking_deadline.description: Last date/time to book a placement in this installment (ISO 8601). After this point, the seller will not accept new bookings.

cancellation_deadline.description: Last date/time to cancel without penalty (ISO 8601). Cancellations after this point may incur fees per the seller's terms.

material_deadlines.description: Stages for creative material submission. Items MUST be in chronological order by due_at (earliest first). Typical pattern: 'draft' for raw materials the seller will process, 'final' for production-ready assets. Print example: draft artwork then press-ready PDF. Influencer example: talking points then approved script.

external:core/material-deadline.json.title: Material Deadline
external:core/material-deadline.json.description: A deadline for creative material submission. Sellers declare stages to distinguish draft materials (e.g., talking points, raw artwork) from production-ready assets (e.g., approved scripts, press-ready PDFs).

stage.description: Submission stage identifier. Use 'draft' for materials that need seller processing and 'final' for production-ready assets. Sellers may define additional stages.

due_at.description: When materials for this stage are due (ISO 8601)

label.description: What the seller needs at this stage (e.g., 'Talking points and brand guidelines', 'Press-ready PDF with bleed')

external:enums/derivative-type.json.title: Derivative Type
external:enums/derivative-type.json.description: What kind of derivative content an installment represents relative to its source installment. The source installment_id must reference an installment within the same response.

enumDescriptions.clip: Short excerpt from the source installment
enumDescriptions.highlight: Editorially curated best-of segment from the source installment
enumDescriptions.recap: Summary of the source installment's content
enumDescriptions.trailer: Promotional content for the source installment
enumDescriptions.bonus: Supplementary content (behind-the-scenes, extended interviews, deleted segments)

external:enums/response-type.json.title: TMP Response Type
external:enums/response-type.json.description: What the publisher wants back from a TMP context match. Determines the richness level of the buyer's offer response.

enumDescriptions.activation: Binary activation with GAM key-values. Offers identify the package via package_id.
enumDescriptions.catalog_items: Preferred catalog items for rendering. Offers may include catalog item references.
enumDescriptions.creative: Inline creative manifest. Offers include full rendering details.
enumDescriptions.deal: Deal ID for programmatic execution. Offers include deal metadata.

external:enums/uid-type.json.title: UID Type
external:enums/uid-type.json.description: Type of user identifier. Used in audience sync, event logging, and TMP identity match requests to tell the receiver which identity graph to resolve against.

enumDescriptions.rampid: LiveRamp RampID maintained form (XY, 32 bytes on the wire)
enumDescriptions.rampid_derived: LiveRamp RampID derived form (Xi, 48 bytes on the wire)
enumDescriptions.pairid: Publisher Addressable Identity via IAB Tech Lab PAIR protocol
enumDescriptions.hashed_email: SHA-256 hashed email address. Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — unsalted SHA-256 of the email namespace is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries; treat as PII. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.
enumDescriptions.publisher_first_party: Publisher's own first-party identifier, opaque to buyers
enumDescriptions.world_id_nullifier: World ID nullifier — a Sybil-resistant, relying-party-scoped, unlinkable pseudonym. Carries NO personhood or age assertion on its own; trust comes only from an accompanying verified `attestation`, never from this type tag. Distinct from the `world_id` value in the age-verification-method enum, which names a method, not an identifier.
enumDescriptions.other: Other universal ID type (specify in ext)

external:media-buy/get-products-targetin.title: Product Discovery Targeting Resolution
external:media-buy/get-products-targetin.description: Confirmation of hard targeting the seller inferred from natural-language discovery instructions. This is emitted once for the result set or refinement it governs; product-specific differences from an explicit structured overlay remain on Product.targeting_resolution.modifications. The filename remains stable for get_products compatibility.

brief_targeting.description: Structured delivery constraints the seller resolved from explicit hard targeting in the brief. This is the seller's literal interpretation, not a counteroffer: products that cannot honor it are omitted. Sellers MUST emit this confirmation when the interpretation materially affects product eligibility, pricing, or forecasting; otherwise it is a best practice. Unchanged structured targeting_overlay values are not repeated.

external:core/targeting.json.title: Targeting Overlay
external:core/targeting.json.description: Concrete delivery constraints used during product discovery and media-buy execution. Targeting includes both audience eligibility and purchased-inventory selection: geography, demographics, placements, properties, collections, device compatibility, language, keywords, and other explicit controls. Sellers resolve requested outcomes against inherent product scope or selectable execution. A fresh create/update request MUST be applied exactly or rejected; get_products may instead return a request-scoped configured product with sparse, buyer-reviewable targeting_resolution modifications.

x-adcp-validation.description: JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare values across sibling arrays. Conformance tooling MUST reject any place identity present in both geo_places and geo_places_exclude. Catalog version is deliberately not part of place identity: a stable ID cannot be both included and excluded by assigning different versions.

geo_countries.description: Restrict delivery to specific countries. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'DE').

geo_countries_exclude.description: Exclude specific countries from delivery. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'DE').

geo_regions.description: Restrict delivery to exact canonical ISO 3166-2 subdivisions (states, provinces, regions, departments, or other subdivision categories). Unknown identifiers are invalid. At create or update, sellers MUST reject unsupported identifiers and MUST NOT silently widen, drop, or partially apply the list. During get_products, a seller may instead return a sparse, buyer-reviewable targeting_resolution modification for a valid but unsupported requested outcome. Exact internal translation preserves accepted identifiers in package readback.

geo_regions_exclude.description: Exclude exact canonical ISO 3166-2 subdivisions. Support is independent from geo_regions inclusion support. Unknown identifiers and values also present in geo_regions are invalid. At create or update, sellers MUST reject unsupported identifiers and partial application; during get_products, a seller may instead return a sparse, buyer-reviewable targeting_resolution modification for a valid but unsupported requested outcome.

geo_metros.description: Restrict delivery to specific metro areas. Each entry specifies the classification system and target values. Seller must declare supported systems in get_adcp_capabilities.

values.description: Metro codes within the system (e.g., ['501', '602'] for Nielsen DMAs)

geo_metros_exclude.description: Exclude specific metro areas from delivery. Each entry specifies the classification system and excluded values. Seller must declare supported systems in get_adcp_capabilities.

values.description: Metro codes to exclude within the system (e.g., ['501', '602'] for Nielsen DMAs)

geo_postal_areas.description: Restrict delivery to specific postal areas. Prefer the native country + postal system form. The deprecated legacy country-fused postal-system tokens remain accepted for compatibility. Seller must declare supported systems in get_adcp_capabilities.

geo_postal_areas_exclude.description: Exclude specific postal areas from delivery. Prefer the native country + postal system form. The deprecated legacy country-fused postal-system tokens remain accepted for compatibility. Seller must declare supported systems in get_adcp_capabilities.

geo_places.description: Restrict delivery to catalog-backed named places. Values MUST be stable identifiers in the declared system, not display names. Sellers must declare supported systems, countries, and place types in get_adcp_capabilities and reject unsupported entries rather than silently dropping them.

geo_places_exclude.description: Exclude catalog-backed named places. Uses the same identifier-based shape as geo_places. Sellers MUST reject overlap with geo_places for the same country, system, place_type, and value.

daypart_targets.description: Restrict delivery to specific time windows. Each entry specifies days of week and an hour range.

axe_include_segment.description: Deprecated: Use TMP provider fields instead. AXE segment ID to include for targeting.

axe_exclude_segment.description: Deprecated: Use TMP provider fields instead. AXE segment ID to exclude from targeting.

audience_include.description: Restrict delivery to members of these first-party CRM audiences. Only users present in the uploaded lists are eligible. References audience_id values from sync_audiences on the same seller account — audience IDs are not portable across sellers. Not for lookalike expansion — express that intent in the campaign brief. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

audience_exclude.description: Suppress delivery to members of these first-party CRM audiences. Matched users are excluded regardless of other targeting. References audience_id values from sync_audiences on the same seller account — audience IDs are not portable across sellers. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

signal_targeting_groups.description: Basic Boolean grouping for seller-offered signals. v1 supports a required top-level operator 'all' and child groups with operator 'any' for include groups or 'none' for exclusion groups. Example semantics: group 1 any(A, B) plus group 2 none(C, D) means (A OR B) AND NOT (C OR D). Signal entries reference named signal definitions with signal_ref scope 'product' for product-local signal options or scope 'data_provider' for external signals published in adagents.json signals[]. For simple include-only targeting, send one child group with operator 'any'. Sellers SHOULD reject entries that are not available for the product through inline signal_targeting_options or get_signals, are not active for the account, or exceed the product's signal_targeting_allowed/signal_targeting_rules/product terms. Signal targeting limits are product-scoped, not declared in get_adcp_capabilities, because products may be backed by different ad servers. Sellers MUST echo applied signal_targeting_groups on the resulting package state, including fixed/default selections. Sellers MAY return REQUOTE_REQUIRED when a targeting mutation changes commercial terms.

signal_targeting.description: DEPRECATED. Use signal_targeting_groups for package-level signal targeting. Legacy flat signal_targeting remains accepted during the SignalRef migration window but cannot express grouped include/exclude composition or product-scoped pricing.

demographics.description: Canonical demographic audience targeting intent with optional constraints on how age may be determined. This is distinct from age_restriction: demographics selects an audience, while age_restriction expresses a legal eligibility or verification floor. Fresh create/update targeting MUST compile exactly or be rejected. During get_products, a seller may offer a different configured predicate only through sparse targeting_resolution modifications on a distinguishable product_id; selecting that product accepts the alternative. Sellers never silently broaden, narrow, default, drop, or substitute the basis.

property_list.description: Reference to a property list for targeting specific properties within this product. The package runs on the intersection of the product's publisher_properties and this list. Sellers SHOULD return a validation error if the product has property_targeting_allowed: false.

property_list_exclude.description: Reference to a property list whose properties must not carry the buyer's ads. Matched properties are removed from delivery. Use for brand-safety do-not-run lists (apps, sites). Exclude wins on overlap with property_list, and applies regardless of the product's property_targeting_allowed flag. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

collection_list.description: Reference to a collection list for including specific collections (programs, shows) within this product. The package runs on the intersection of matched collections and this list. Use for inclusion-based collection targeting. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

collection_list_exclude.description: Reference to a collection list for excluding specific collections (programs, shows) from this product. Matched collections must not carry the buyer's ads. Use for brand safety do-not-air lists. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

placement_selection.description: Purchased placement selection within the product. This constrains package inventory; it is distinct from creative_assignments[].placement_refs, which only route individual creatives within the purchased set. On create, mode selected supplies the complete selected set and mode default uses the product default. On update, the surrounding targeting_overlay replacement semantics apply.

age_restriction.description: Age restriction for compliance. Use for legal requirements (alcohol, gambling), not audience targeting.

verification_required.description: Whether verified age (not inferred) is required for compliance

accepted_methods.description: Accepted verification methods. If omitted, any method the platform supports is acceptable.

device_platform.description: Restrict to specific platforms. Use for technical compatibility (app only works on iOS). Values from Sec-CH-UA-Platform standard, extended for CTV.

device_platform_exclude.description: Exclude specific operating-system platforms from delivery. When a platform appears in both device_platform and device_platform_exclude, exclusion wins. Sellers MUST reject a request they cannot enforce rather than silently dropping the exclusion.

device_type.description: Restrict to specific device form factors. Use for campaigns targeting hardware categories rather than operating systems (e.g., mobile-only promotions, CTV campaigns).

device_type_exclude.description: Exclude specific device form factors from delivery (e.g., exclude CTV for app-install campaigns).

browser.description: Restrict delivery to specific canonical browser families in the impression delivery and rendering environment, not the post-click landing-page browser. Values MUST NOT be inferred solely from operating system, device, web/mobile-web inventory, or placement. Values in this array use OR semantics. When browser is supplied, families not listed are ineligible: other includes a seller-recognized family that is not explicitly enumerated, while unknown includes a browser the seller cannot classify into a recognized family. When the same family appears in browser and browser_exclude, exclusion wins. Browser and device constraints intersect; a seller that cannot enforce the exact combination MUST exclude or explicitly reconfigure the product during discovery and MUST reject it at create or update rather than silently widening delivery. Browser versions and seller-native IDs are intentionally unsupported.

browser_exclude.description: Exclude specific canonical browser families from delivery. other excludes seller-recognized families that are not explicitly enumerated; unknown excludes browsers the seller cannot classify into a recognized family. When the same family appears in browser and browser_exclude, exclusion wins. Sellers MUST reject a request they cannot enforce rather than silently dropping the exclusion.

store_catchments.description: Target users within store catchment areas from a synced store catalog. Each entry references a store-type catalog and optionally narrows to specific stores or catchment zones.

catalog_id.description: Synced store-type catalog ID from sync_catalogs.

store_ids.description: Filter to specific stores within the catalog. Omit to target all stores.

catchment_ids.description: Catchment zone IDs to target (e.g., 'walk', 'drive'). Omit to target all catchment zones.

geo_proximity.description: Target users within travel time, distance, or a custom boundary around arbitrary geographic points. Multiple entries use OR semantics — a user within range of any listed point is eligible. For campaigns targeting 10+ locations, consider using store_catchments with a location catalog instead. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). Required for travel_time and radius methods.

lng.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). Required for travel_time and radius methods.

label.description: Human-readable label for this entry (e.g., 'Düsseldorf', 'Heathrow Airport', 'Primary trade area').

travel_time.description: Travel time limit for isochrone calculation. The platform resolves this to a geographic boundary based on actual transportation networks.

transport_mode.description: Transportation mode for isochrone calculation. Required when travel_time is provided.

radius.description: Simple radius from the point. The platform draws a circle of this distance around the coordinates.

geometry.description: Pre-computed GeoJSON geometry defining the proximity boundary. Use when the buyer has already calculated isochrones (via TravelTime, Mapbox, etc.) or has custom boundaries. When geometry is provided, lat/lng are not required.

coordinates.description: GeoJSON coordinates array. For Polygon: array of linear rings. For MultiPolygon: array of polygons.

language.description: Restrict to users with specific language preferences using canonical BCP 47 language ranges. Each buyer range is evaluated against a user's language-preference tag with RFC 4647 section 3.3.1 Basic Filtering: 'fr' matches 'fr', 'fr-CA', and 'fr-FR', while 'fr-CA' matches 'fr-CA' and more-specific descendants but not 'fr' or 'fr-FR'. Values use OR logic.

keyword_targets.description: Keyword targeting for search and retail media platforms. Restricts delivery to queries matching the specified keywords. Each keyword is identified by the tuple (keyword, match_type) — the same keyword string with different match types are distinct targets. Sellers SHOULD reject duplicate (keyword, match_type) pairs within a single request. Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

bid_price.description: Per-keyword bid price, denominated in the same currency as the package's pricing option. Overrides the package-level bid_price for this keyword. Inherits the max_bid interpretation from the pricing option: when max_bid is true, this is the keyword's bid ceiling; when false, this is the exact bid. If omitted, the package bid_price applies.

negative_keywords.description: Keywords to exclude from delivery. Queries matching these keywords will not trigger the ad. Each negative keyword is identified by the tuple (keyword, match_type). Seller must declare support in get_adcp_capabilities.

allOf.description: Unknown-age delivery cannot satisfy a minimum-age eligibility policy. When demographic audience targeting and age_restriction are both present, include_unknown must be false.

A legal verification requirement always narrows demographic targeting. When the buyer supplies accepted_bases and age_restriction requires verification, verified must be accepted; otherwise the constraints have an empty intersection and the request is invalid.

external:core/postal-area.json.title: Postal Area
external:core/postal-area.json.description: Postal area values. Prefer the native country + postal system form. Deprecated legacy country-fused postal-system tokens remain accepted for compatibility.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the postal values.

values.description: Postal codes within the country and system.

system.description: Deprecated country-fused postal code system (e.g., 'us_zip', 'gb_outward'). Prefer country + postal-system.

values.description: Postal codes within the legacy system.

external:core/geo-place-area.json.title: Geographic Place Area
external:core/geo-place-area.json.description: A catalog-backed named place target. Values are stable identifiers in the declared system. Entries within geo_places form a union; different geographic inclusion dimensions intersect. value_labels are diagnostic only and MUST NOT be used to resolve targeting.

x-adcp-validation.description: Every value_labels key MUST also appear in values. JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express this sibling-field key membership constraint, so conformance tooling must enforce it.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code containing the place.

system_version.description: Optional exact catalog version from the seller's declared supported_versions. When omitted, the seller applies catalog.current_version and MUST echo that version on persisted package state.

values.description: Stable place identifiers in the declared system. Display names are not valid targeting values.

value_labels.description: Optional human-readable diagnostic labels keyed by identifiers present in values. Extra keys are a conformance error. Labels are non-authoritative and MUST NOT be used to resolve or apply targeting.

external:core/daypart-target.json.title: Daypart Target
external:core/daypart-target.json.description: A time window for daypart targeting. Specifies days of week and an hour range. start_hour is inclusive, end_hour is exclusive (e.g., 6-10 = 6:00am to 10:00am). Follows the Google Ads AdScheduleInfo / DV360 DayPartTargeting pattern.

days.description: Days of week this window applies to. Use multiple days for compact targeting (e.g., monday-friday in one object).

end_hour.description: End hour (exclusive), 1-24 in 24-hour format. 10 = 10:00am, 24 = midnight. Must be greater than start_hour.

label.description: Optional human-readable name for this time window (e.g., 'Morning Drive', 'Prime Time')

external:enums/day-of-week.json.title: Day of Week
external:enums/day-of-week.json.description: Days of the week for daypart targeting

external:core/package-signal-targeting-g.title: Package Signal Targeting Groups
external:core/package-signal-targeting-g.description: Top-level basic Boolean composition for package signal targeting. The groups-level operator is required; v1 supports operator 'all', meaning every child group must be satisfied. This represents the portable baseline: (any of include group 1) AND (any of include group 2) AND NOT (any of exclude group N).

operator.description: Groups-level operator. Required even though v1 only supports 'all': every child group must be satisfied.

groups.description: Signal targeting groups to evaluate. Use operator 'any' for include groups and 'none' for exclusion groups.

external:core/package-signal-targeting-g.title: Package Signal Targeting Group
external:core/package-signal-targeting-g.description: A basic Boolean group of package-level signal targeting entries. 'any' means the user must match at least one signal in the group. 'none' means the user must match none of the signals in the group. Use groups for portable include/exclude composition such as (A OR B) AND NOT (C OR D).

operator.description: How to evaluate the signals in this group. 'any' is an OR include group. 'none' is an exclusion group equivalent to NOT (A OR B OR C).

signals.description: Signal targeting entries evaluated by this group. Each entry uses the package signal targeting shape, including signal_ref, value expression, and optional pricing, execution-handle, or activation fields.

external:core/package-signal-targeting.j.title: Package Signal Targeting
external:core/package-signal-targeting.j.description: Buy-time selection of one seller-offered signal inside a package signal targeting group. The signal_ref uses scope 'product' for a product-local signal option, scope 'data_provider' for a signal defined in a data provider's published adagents.json signals[], or scope 'signal_source' for a source-native signal that is not published in adagents.json signals[]. The selected product's inline Product.signal_targeting_options, get_signals feed when inline options are omitted, and signal_targeting_rules define buy-time eligibility.
